description: A linear frequency shifter for pitch voltages: it converts each pitch to a frequency, adds a fixed number of hertz to it and converts back, on nine independent pairs of jacks

params.text: Sets how many hertz are added to every pitch, over the span chosen by the range knob and the same amount either side of nothing
Scales the frequency modulation input; the setting is raised to the fourth power, so almost all of the travel is at the top of the knob
Chooses the span of the shift knob: plus and minus 10, 20, 40, 80, 160, 320, 640, 1280 or 2560Hz. A new module starts on 160Hz.

inputs.text: A pitch to shift, one volt per octave
Adds to the frequency shift while the module runs, scaled by the frequency modulation knob; at the knob's top 1V here adds 261.63Hz, which is one times the frequency of C4

outputs.text: The shifted pitch from the input beside it, one volt per octave, and never lower than -10V

notes: the shift is in hertz and not in semitones, so a chord fed through it comes out inharmonic: the same shift moves a low note much further in pitch than a high one.
each output is only written while it is patched, and it takes its channel count from the input beside it, so an output with nothing on its own input carries nothing.
